Definition: from a derivative of G1131; to strip, i.e. (reflexively) go poorly clad:--be naked.
BiblicalUsage: gymnēteúō means to be naked, without clothing. In 1 Corinthians 4:11, the text says "and are naked."
TheologicalSignificance: I read gymnēteúō plainly — it means to be naked, without clothing, and I do not build a doctrine on it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
